title: Computational Game Theory
after: after the Computational Game Theory lecture slides
dek: What a rational choice is when other people are choosing too, how to find one, and how hard that is to compute. Written for someone who has never seen a payoff matrix.
blurb: Preferences and expected utility, normal form games and Nash equilibrium, mixed strategies, game trees, repeated and evolutionary games, zero-sum games, and win-lose games as complexity classes.
colophon: Based on the lecture slides for Computational Game Theory (Department of Computer Science, Oxford), seven lectures and three tutorial sheets. Numbering of results is added here, since the slides number nothing; the small numbers in the margin are slide numbers. The background boxes, figures, proofs marked as additions and exercises are new; errors in them are new too.
